title: Universal Scaling of Conditional Mutual Information in Classical Stochastic Dynamics
authors: Songlei Wang, Chenguang Liang, Zhi-Cheng Yang
abstract: Conditional mutual information (CMI) characterizes dependence between two regions conditioned on an intervening buffer. Its characteristic decay length, the Markov length, has recently been identified as a diverging length scale at mixed-state phase transitions. Here, we investigate CMI dynamics in one-dimensional classical stochastic models and propose a universal scaling form for systems whose Markov length diverges with time. We derive this form in the inactive phase of parity-conserving directed percolation, where domain-wall coarsening generates a growing length scale and a self-similar probability distribution. We introduce a Hankel-based truncation scheme that enables matrix-product-state simulations at long times and over large spatial regions. Using this method, we verify the proposed scaling both in the inactive phase and at the nonequilibrium critical point, where the dynamical critical exponent governs Markov-length growth. More broadly, the same scaling form captures cases in which collective inference sets the diverging Markov length. Despite these distinct mechanisms, the CMI between fixed microscopic regions exhibits a common scaling dimension of two. Finally, we extend this framework to temporal CMI, establishing an analogous relation between the strength of conditional dependence in time domain and its characteristic memory time.
summary: This work establishes a universal scaling law for the Conditional Mutual Information (CMI) in classical stochastic systems whose correlation length diverges over time. By applying advanced MPS simulation techniques, the authors verify this scaling in models like directed percolation and the SSEP. This provides a general information-theoretic tool to characterize critical dynamics and memory effects in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the universal scaling form of Conditional Mutual Information (CMI) in classical stochastic dynamics, particularly when the characteristic Markov length diverges with time.
main_result: A universal scaling form for CMI is derived and verified for systems exhibiting diverging Markov lengths, such as in the inactive phase of directed percolation and in temporal CMI for the SSEP.
method: The authors employ advanced numerical techniques, including a novel Hankel-based truncation scheme for Matrix Product States (MPS), to simulate CMI dynamics in 1D classical stochastic models.
model_or_system: The study focuses on one-dimensional classical stochastic models, including parity-conserving directed percolation (PCDP) and the Symmetric Simple Exclusion Process (SSEP). These models exhibit continuous absorbing-state phase transitions.
key_observables: Conditional Mutual Information (CMI), the Markov length ($\xi_M$), and the domain-wall density ($ho(t)$).
important_parameters: The analysis covers different regimes of PCDP (inactive phase, critical point) and temporal correlations in SSEP, with key parameters including coupling strengths ($Q$) and time ($t$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the proposed scaling form holds universally for classical stochastic processes where the Markov length diverges, and that the Hankel scheme accurately captures long-time CMI tails.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the tripartition geometry for CMI calculation and compare the accuracy of CMI profiles obtained using the Hankel-based truncation versus conventional canonical truncation in the DP model.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces CMI and the concept of the Markov length. It then derives and verifies the universal scaling form using PCDP dynamics in its inactive phase and at the critical point. Finally, it extends the framework to temporal CMI, applying it to the SSEP.
why_interesting: The concept of CMI and its scaling behavior provides a powerful, information-theoretic diagnostic tool to characterize non-equilibrium critical dynamics and long-range correlations in classical many-body systems, bridging statistical mechanics with information theory.

FIG. 4. Schmidt weights enter observables in quantum and probability MPS differently. (a) A diagonal one-site observ- able in a quantum MPS is evaluated through a double-layer contraction, which weights the virtual sectors through Λ2 and aligns their contributions with the Schmidt ordering. (b) The corresponding classical observable in a probability iMPS is evaluated through a single-layer contraction. The bond spec- trum then enters linearly together with the left and right en- vironments, so a canonical weight alone does not determine the importance of the associated virtual direction.
